Não aprovamos expansão. Recomendamos fase limitada de verificação, antes de decisão final. Essa proposta busca usar o alerta como triagem, não como prova de economia. O hardware e o treinamento devem ser avaliados como custos reais, com subsídio condicionado. A recomendação é equilibrada porque 11 vazamentos confirmados mostram potencial operacional, mas quatro falhas, três imóveis inacessíveis e revisão de privacidade incompleta impedem decisão ampla.

No piloto P-004, 120 medidores funcionaram por 6 semanas. Dezoito medidores geraram alertas de vazamento. ## Recommendation

Proposal: The board of fictional Brookmere Water Utility should authorize a gated, six-week validation phase limited to the existing 120 meters, rather than approve expansion. Authorization would be conditional on a finance assessment, an operational protocol, and privacy clearance. P-004 demonstrates verified leak detection, but does not establish improved detection, water savings, or financial value relative to current practice. The grant deadline warrants prompt evaluation, not a premature purchase commitment.

## Evidence

P-004 covered 120 meters for six weeks. Eighteen meters produced leak alerts: technicians verified 11 real leaks, identified four sensor faults, and could not access three properties. Thus, 11 of 18 alerted meters had verified leaks; the inaccessible properties remain unresolved, not confirmed false alarms. The pilot provides no basis for estimating how many leaks went undetected.

The prior six-week comparison recorded eight verified leaks. Although P-004 recorded three more, the comparison involved a different neighborhood and was not randomized. Neighborhood differences and other uncontrolled factors prevent attributing that difference to the technology.

Hardware costs USD 24,000 and training costs USD 3,000, totaling USD 27,000. The grant can cover USD 9,600, or 40% of hardware only, leaving USD 17,400 of those stated costs if awarded. This excludes unestimated ongoing fees and any additional phase costs. No water-savings measurement is available, so neither payback nor net benefit can yet be calculated.

## Risks

Sensor faults may consume technician capacity, while inaccessible properties leave alert accuracy uncertain. Small scale and short duration limit confidence in performance elsewhere. Privacy review is incomplete, and retaining hourly readings for 90 days creates an unresolved governance issue. The grant expires on 2026-11-15; eligibility and timing constraints could undermine the assumed contribution. Expansion has not been approved.

## Next steps

Proposal: The Finance Director should own a documented total-cost assessment, including recurring charges, fieldwork, maintenance, and grant conditions, and present funded and unfunded scenarios before any commitment.

Proposal: The Operations Director should own the proposed validation phase, seek access to the three unresolved properties, investigate the four sensor faults, and define consistent verification procedures. The protocol should measure response workload, confirmed leaks, and water savings using documented baselines, while explicitly reporting uncertainty and comparison limitations.

Proposal: The Privacy Officer should complete the review before further data collection, document access controls and retention justification, and recommend whether shorter retention or other safeguards are necessary.

Proposal: These owners should jointly submit a costed protocol and board decision timetable before 2026-11-15. The board should approve success criteria in advance and require a final evidence report before considering expansion; unresolved privacy or affordability concerns should trigger deferral.
